Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.audioplayer

Class CdRipBackend

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.audioplayer.CdRipBackend
public final class CdRipBackend extends Object
The AWT-free CD-ripping seam. Ripping a physical audio CD is genuinely native to no part of the JDK - there is no in-JDK CD-DA reader and no bundled MP3 encoder - so, exactly like AudioBackend's codec split and
invalid reference 
RecorderBackend
's ffmpeg handoff, this backend builds the precise command lines for real external tools and leaves the thin, guarded process launch to AudioPlayerPanel.

The pipeline is: read the disc TOC (cdparanoia -Q, fallback cd-info) to learn the track count and offsets; extract each selected track to WAV (cdparanoia, or ffmpeg -f audiocd); then, when the user asked for something other than a straight 44.1 kHz WAV, encode / resample with ffmpeg (preferred) or lame.

Every method here is pure and side-effect free - no process is started, no device is opened - so the whole command / format table is unit-testable headless. defaultDevice() is the only method that touches the filesystem, and only to test which device nodes exist; the pure defaultDevice(Predicate) variant is what the tests exercise.

    • readTocCommand

      public static List<String> readTocCommand(String ripper, String device)
      Builds the command that reads the disc TOC. cdparanoia prints the TOC to stderr with -Q; cd-info prints it to stdout.
      Parameters:
      ripper - the ripper executable (e.g. cdparanoia)
      device - the CD device node (blank means the tool's default)
      Returns:
      the argument list, or empty when ripper is blank

    • ripWavCommand

      public static List<String> ripWavCommand(String ripper, String device, int track, String outWav)
      Builds the command that extracts track from the disc to a WAV file. cdparanoia is preferred (error-corrected); ffmpeg -f audiocd is the fallback when cdparanoia is absent.
      Parameters:
      ripper - the ripper executable (e.g. cdparanoia / ffmpeg)
      device - the CD device node (blank means the tool's default)
      track - the 1-based track number to extract
      outWav - the destination .wav path
      Returns:
      the argument list, or empty when a required input is blank or the track number is out of range

    • encodeCommand

      public static List<String> encodeCommand(String encoder, String inWav, String outFile, CdRipBackend.Format format, int sampleRate, int bitrate)
      Builds the command that encodes / resamples inWav into outFile in the requested format. WAV output only needs a step when the target rate differs from the CD-native 44100 Hz; MP3 always encodes. lame handles MP3 only - a WAV resample with lame is unsupported and yields an empty command so the caller can pick ffmpeg.
      Parameters:
      encoder - the encoder executable (e.g. ffmpeg / lame)
      inWav - the source WAV path
      outFile - the destination path
      format - the target CdRipBackend.Format
      sampleRate - the target sampling rate in Hz (normalised internally)
      bitrate - the MP3 bitrate in kbps (normalised internally; ignored for WAV)
      Returns:
      the argument list, or empty when a required input is blank or the encoder cannot produce the requested format
